skill.name: hyperframes-cli
skill.description: Guide agents through HyperFrames CLI workflows for project setup, linting, visual inspection, preview, rendering, transcription, text-to-speech, and troubleshooting.
skill.summary: Run HyperFrames CLI workflows for video projects, validation, preview, rendering, audio transcription, text-to-speech, and environment checks.
skill.author: heygen-com

security_audit.summary: The static backtick alerts are mixed: many are Markdown formatting false positives, but several entries intentionally direct agents to run npx hyperframes. The main risk is expected external CLI execution, with a higher concern that init may install additional AI coding skills.

remediation.suggestion: Document the trusted package source and recommend pinned versions or local project dependencies before running CLI commands.

remediation.issue: Init can install AI coding skills
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation and list every installed skill before invoking init modes that change agent configuration.

remediation.issue: Preview and documentation commands can open local services or browser windows
remediation.suggestion: Tell agents to ask before starting preview servers, opening browsers, or running upgrade and docs commands.

static_findings.snippet: Everything runs through `npx hyperframes`. Requires Node.js >= 22 and FFmpeg.
Lint and inspect before preview. `lint` catches missing `data-composition-id`, overlapping tracks, a
`init` creates the right file structure, copies media, transcribes audio with Whisper, and installs
Lints `index.html` and all files in `compositions/`. Reports errors (must fix), warnings (should fix
Use this after `lint` and `validate`, especially for compositions with speech bubbles, cards, captio
Errors should be fixed before rendering. Warnings are surfaced for agent review; add `--strict` to f
`npx hyperframes layout` remains available as a compatibility alias for the same visual inspection p
Treat `index.html` as source-code context only. It is fine to link it as an
| `--quality`    | draft, standard, high | standard                   | draft for iterating
| `--format`     | mp4, webm             | mp4                        | WebM supports transparency
| `--workers`    | 1-8 or auto           | auto                       | Each spawns Chrome
| `--strict`     | flag                  | off                        | Fail on lint errors
| `--strict-all` | flag                  | off                        | Fail on errors AND warnings
**Quality guidance:** `draft` while iterating, `standard` for review, `high` for final delivery.
Run `doctor` first if rendering fails. Common issues: missing FFmpeg, missing Chrome, low memory.

content.value_statement: Video projects need repeatable setup, validation, preview, and rendering steps. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through HyperFrames CLI workflows.
actual_capabilities: Scaffolds HyperFrames projects with examples, video inputs, audio inputs, or non-interactive setup.
Runs lint checks for index files, compositions, timeline registration, and layout problems.
Guides visual inspection of rendered compositions over selected timeline samples.
Starts local preview workflows and returns the correct Studio project URL format.
Renders MP4 or WebM outputs with quality, FPS, Docker, GPU, and worker options.
Supports transcription, text-to-speech, environment checks, browser management, and benchmarking.
limitations: Requires Node.js 22 or newer and FFmpeg in the local environment.
Depends on the external HyperFrames CLI package and its installed version.
Rendering can launch Chrome and may use significant CPU, memory, or GPU resources.
Some commands may need user approval before opening browsers or changing local files.

use_cases.title: Create a Video Project
use_cases.description: Set up a new HyperFrames project with the right template, media inputs, and validation steps.

use_cases.title: Validate Motion Layouts
use_cases.description: Check compositions for missing timeline data, overflow, clipping, and canvas layout issues before rendering.

use_cases.title: Render and Troubleshoot Output
use_cases.description: Choose render settings, diagnose missing dependencies, and prepare review or final video files.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a HyperFrames project for my video. Pick a suitable starter template and explain the next validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Check Composition Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Lint and visually inspect this HyperFrames project. Summarize errors, warnings, and the fixes needed before preview.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Review Render
prompt_templates.prompt: Preview this project, confirm the Studio URL, then render a standard review video with practical settings.

prompt_templates.title: Automate a Production Pass
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a strict HyperFrames workflow for final delivery, including inspection, render settings, transcription, and environment checks.

output_examples.input: Set up a product promo video from a source clip and narration track.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a template, setup mode, media handling steps, and follow-up lint and inspection checks.

output_examples.input: My captions overflow during animation and the render looks wrong.
output_examples.output: The skill focuses on lint results, visual inspection samples, overflow causes, and targeted layout fixes before rendering again.

output_examples.input: Prepare a final transparent video with high quality settings.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines preview confirmation, render format choice, quality settings, dependency checks, and final output review.

best_practices: Run lint and visual inspection before every preview or render.
Use draft quality during iteration and high quality only for final delivery.
Share the Studio project URL instead of the source HTML file path.
anti_patterns: Do not render before fixing lint errors and visible layout problems.
Do not treat index.html as the preview surface for users.
Do not run upgrade, browser, or init commands without clear user approval.

faq.question: What does this skill help automate?
faq.answer: It guides HyperFrames CLI setup, validation, preview, rendering, transcription, speech generation, and troubleshooting workflows.

faq.question: Does it create video content by itself?
faq.answer: No. It guides CLI workflows and project checks. The HyperFrames project and local tools produce the output.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Why does it need external commands?
faq.answer: The skill is built around the HyperFrames CLI, so useful workflows require local command execution.

faq.question: Can it inspect visual layout issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides visual inspection for overflow, clipping, canvas escapes, and tight typography problems.

faq.question: What should users approve first?
faq.answer: Users should approve commands that install packages, install skills, open browsers, update tools, or write project files.
